title: governor config file
description: The shape of governor's config file, .github/dispatch.json, for an editor to complete and check keys while the file is written. It covers the shape only: it leaves out the rules across keys and the checks on a prompt's text or a prompt file's path, and cannot read prompt files, so a file it accepts can still be refused. The config check, the reusable workflow .github/workflows/config-check.yml in t-d-d/gh-governor, is the full check.

$schema.description: The URL of this file's JSON Schema, for an editor to describe and check each key. Governor ignores it. Use the schema at the commit the config check is pinned to, and bump both together.

environment.description: The claude.ai cloud environment the repo's sessions start in: its name as `/remote-env` lists it, or its ID. A public repo should use the name.

ready.description: Every label a ready ticket carries.

claim.description: The label governor claims a ticket with before its session starts. It is created in a repo that lacks it. A ticket carrying it is never picked up.

claimRemoves.description: The ready labels the claim takes off, and a failed launch puts back. Default none.

exclude.description: Labels that keep a ticket out: a ticket carrying any of them is never picked up, and a blocker's close starts no session for it. It cannot name a ready label. Default `["type: prd"]`. A hold label, one that marks a ticket as needing a person or staying not ready (`mode: human`, say), belongs here, or a blocker's close starts a session to rewrite that ticket's spec.

labels.description: The labels governor reads and writes on tickets: `ready`, `claim`, `claimRemoves` and `exclude`.

features.description: The switches that turn governor's features on, each `true` or `false`. A switch left out is off.

pickup.description: A session per ready ticket, picked up on its label, on the close of its last open blocker, and on the sweep at the interval `pickup.sweepHours` sets.

summons.description: A session per `@claude` remark, and a dispatch started by hand.

prMessages.description: Messages into the session a PR names, or the newest live session holding its branch.

subscribeMessages.description: Messages to sessions subscribed by a `governor:subscribe` line, and to an issue's filer. A filer hears a `deployed:` label on its issue only through a subscribe line for `deploys`.

redScheduledRun.description: A fresh session on a scheduled run on the default branch that went red.

unblocked.description: What a blocker's close does to a ticket that is not ready to pick up: a comment when the blocker closed as not planned, a message to a claimed ticket's session, and the spec work on a not-ready ticket. The session whose link ends the ticket's body owns it and is asked to rewrite its own spec; a fresh session rewrites it only where the body names no session or that session is archived, so nobody takes a ticket from its owner. A file that still sets the older `mergeHandoff` reads as this.

ciMessages.description: A red CI run tells the sessions of the merges it may blame. Needs `workflows.ci`.

deployMessages.description: A shipping job, or a red deploy, tells the sessions of the merges it shipped.

branchRunMessages.description: A run dispatched on a branch tells the session that wrote its commit.

conflicts.description: A merge into the default branch tells each PR it left conflicted.

deployedLabels.description: A shipping job labels the tickets it shipped `deployed: <target>`. Needs `deployMessages`.

prReview.description: The PR review, run from the `review` section.

heartbeat.description: Governor records each fire on the issue the `heartbeat` section names: a line for pickup and one per periodic. In the older shape with a `marker`, the hourly sweep stamps the issue's `last-run:` line instead.

periodics.description: A session per periodic in the `periodics` list, each time its day limit passes or one of its counts is reached.

hooks.description: A session on a hook's prompt when a signed request fires one of the hooks the `hooks` list holds. A fire while the hook's last session is open goes into that session as a message.

waits.description: When a ticket's `Blocked until:` date passes and it is not ready, one comment saying the wait ended, and, if `unblocked` is on, its spec work, which goes to its owner first as a blocker's close does. Every session governor starts is told how to make a ticket wait. The hold itself needs no switch.

signOff.description: Governor archives an idle session in the repo whose last reply ends `Signing off.`, and a message about a close or a deploy, with nothing else open, asks the session to sign off.

ticketReviews.description: Each review the `ticketReviews` list holds comments on a ticket it selects, when the ticket is opened, reopened or has its body edited: whether it passes, waits for an edit, or waits for a person.

prompts.description: Replacement wording for the instruction in each kind of message, keyed by kind.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

workflows.description: What the repo's workflows are to governor: `ci`, `triage` and `tags`.

ci.description: The CI workflow's file, under `.github/workflows/`. A red run of it tells the sessions of the merges it may blame. Without it, no run is CI.

triage.description: The deploy targets whose failure starts one fresh session, rather than messages to the sessions of the merges it shipped. Default none.

tags.description: The tag each deploy target's deploy moves, keyed by target, which deploy messages name. Default none.

review.description: The PR review's settings: its checklist, and the lists it checks a PR against. Needed when `prReview` is on.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

checklist.description: Required. The review model's system prompt, after governor's fixed frame and before a suffix naming what the code decided: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }.

humanOnly.description: Paths a PR may not change without a person: a PR changing a matching path waits for one, unless every ticket it closes carries one of the entry's `unless` labels and the PR is not from a session governor started. Default none.

glob.description: The paths a PR may not change without a person, as a glob.

reason.description: Why a person must see a change to these paths, which the review says.

unless.description: Labels that waive the wait when every ticket the PR closes carries one and passes the review's ticket checks. They waive nothing for a PR from a session governor started. Default none.

tickets.description: The label rules every ticket the PR closes must meet: `require` and `forbid`.

require.description: Rules each ticket the PR closes meets by carrying one of the rule's labels, unless it carries one of its `unless` labels. Default none.

labels.description: The labels the rule is about.

unless.description: Labels that waive the rule for a ticket carrying one of them. Default none.

forbid.description: Rules each ticket the PR closes meets by carrying none of the rule's labels, unless it carries one of its `unless` labels. Default none.

labels.description: The labels the rule is about.

unless.description: Labels that waive the rule for a ticket carrying one of them. Default none.

quote.description: Globs of changed files the review model reads whole, at the merge base and at the head. Only a modified file is quoted: one added, removed or renamed waits for a person. A `!` entry takes a path back out. Default none.

decides.description: Labels of a ticket that may decide a quoted file's change: its body's first line, `Constraint now lives at <path>, …`, names the files it decides, which then pass unread. Default none.

dependabot.description: Globs of the manifests a Dependabot PR may change and pass with no model. Default none.

requireChecks.description: Checks the review treats as required, beside any the default branch requires on GitHub: a name, which a check run from any App or a commit status context meets, or `{ "name", "app" }`, which only that App's check run of the name meets. One red on the PR's head fails the review for a push; one not finished, or not posted, holds the review with `governor` in progress until it ends. A name GitHub also requires counts once, and the review's own `governor` check is left out. Default none.

app.description: The slug of the GitHub App that must post it, such as `github-actions` or `github-code-scanning`: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, the last part of its `github.com/apps/<slug>` page. A run of the name from any other App, and a commit status of the name, does not count.

waitForCi.description: Whether the review waits for the `workflows.ci` run at the PR's head: one red fails it for a push, one not finished, or none at the head, holds it with `governor` in progress. Set it false where the CI workflow does not run on pull requests, such as one that runs only on a push to the default branch; the review then reads no workflow runs, and still reads the required checks and `requireChecks`. A red CI run on the default branch still drives `ciMessages`. Default true.

merge.description: Whether a pass merges the PR. With false, a pass posts its comment and a success check, and the owner merges. Default true.

heartbeat.description: `{ "issue": <number> }`: the issue governor records every fire on, under the `<!-- governor:heartbeat -->` marker its body must carry. The older `{ "issue": <number>, "marker": "<!-- … -->" }` keeps one `last-run:` line under the repo's own marker, which the hourly sweep updates. Needed when `heartbeat` is on.

issue.description: The number of the issue governor records its fires on. Its body must already carry the marker, or governor writes nothing into it.

marker.description: The older shape: the repo's own marker, an HTML comment on one line, under which the hourly sweep keeps one `last-run:` line. Without it, governor keeps a line for pickup and one per periodic under `<!-- governor:heartbeat -->`.

waits.description: `{ "issue": <number> }`: the wait ticket, which each waiting ticket is linked as blocked by while it waits, so its sidebar shows the wait. Read only with `waits` on. Without it, governor links nothing.

issue.description: The number of the wait ticket: governor links each waiting ticket as blocked by it, and removes the link when the wait ends. An issue can block at most 50.

pickup.description: `{ "sweepHours": <number>, "by": [ … ] }`: how many whole hours the hourly fire leaves between two sweeps of the repo's ready tickets, at least one, default one; and `by`, the retired name of `trust.task`, which governor reads as it.

sweepHours.description: How many whole hours the hourly fire leaves between two sweeps of the repo's ready tickets, at least one. Default one, which sweeps at every fire.

by.description: Retired: read as `trust.task`, and refused beside it. Whose tickets pickup may start, and whose issue or PR a summons may start a session on: the `author_association` values GitHub gives the person who opened it. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. Where a repo lists any other value, a ready label on such a ticket counts only when a person other than its author, or governor's own App, added it last.

trust.description: `{ "start": [ … ], "auto": [ … ], "task": [ … ], "relay": [ … ], "review": [ … ] }`: whose GitHub text governor acts on, by `author_association`. `start` is who may set work going, by readying a ticket or writing a summons, default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, which a repo may narrow and never widen. `auto` is whose issues and PRs governor sets going by itself, default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. `task` is whose issue or PR may become work when a person readies it or summons a session on it, default the same three. `relay` is whose text may reach a running session, default those three and `BOT`. `review` is whose pull requests the PR review reads, default the three.

start.description: Who may set work going, by `author_association`: whose ready label counts, and whose summons starts a session. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. A repo may narrow it, never widen it: any other value, and `BOT`, is refused.

auto.description: Whose issues and PRs governor sets going by itself, with no person choosing the ticket, by `author_association`: a spec session or owner message when a ticket's wait ends or its blocker closes, a periodic's issue counts and listings, and the conflicts check. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, narrowed to fit `task` (or `pickup.by`), `relay` and `review` where the file sets them. `BOT` is refused.

task.description: Whose issue or PR may become work when a person sets it going, by `author_association`: pickup starts a ready ticket, and a summons starts a session, only where its author is listed. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`, narrowed to fit `relay` and `review` where the file sets them. `BOT` is refused. The older `pickup.by` is read as this list, and a file may not set both.

relay.description: Whose text may reach a session that is already running, by `author_association`, with `BOT` for any account GitHub marks as a bot: their comments and reviews, and a session link or `governor:subscribe` line in the body of an issue or PR they open. An event such as a label, a close or a push is judged by the author of the issue or PR it is on. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR` and `BOT`, less any of the first three a `review` the file sets leaves out. Governor's own App is never judged.

review.description: Whose pull requests governor's PR review reads, by `author_association`, with `BOT` for any account GitHub marks as a bot. A pull request by an author it leaves out gets a `neutral` `governor` check, and a person merges it. Dependabot's pull requests are read by `review.dependabot` whatever it says. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`.

periodics.description: The recurring sessions governor starts on a day limit, or on a count of merges, issues opened or issues closed. At least one when the `periodics` switch is on.

name.description: The periodic's name: one line, unique in the file. Its session is named after it, and governor keys its record by it.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: What the periodic's session runs: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Governor adds a line under it giving the last fire's time, and lists what each count counted since then.

days.description: Required. The day limit, in whole days, at least one: the periodic is due on the sweep nearest that many days after its last fire.

counts.description: Counts that bring the periodic due before its day limit, once any reaches its number since the last fire: `merges`, `issuesOpened` and `issuesClosed`. At its day limit, a periodic whose counts counted nothing starts no session.

merges.description: Pull requests merged into the default branch since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

issuesOpened.description: Issues opened since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

issuesClosed.description: Issues closed since the last fire that bring the periodic due, a whole number of at least one.

gapHours.description: The fewest whole hours between two of the periodic's runs, at least one. A count reached inside the gap fires on the first event or sweep after it.

connectors.description: The claude.ai connectors the periodic's session needs, each named once by its name in the account's connector list. A periodic naming any starts as a run of a routine governor keeps for it, with those connectors attached and no others.

hooks.description: The sessions an outside system starts with a signed request, each with an optional `perHour` cap on fires. At least one when the `hooks` switch is on.

name.description: The hook's name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the file. It ends the hook's URL, and its session is named after it.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

prompt.description: What the hook's session runs: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Governor adds lines under it saying which hook fired and when, and quoting the caller's text as the caller's data.

keyVersion.description: Required. The version of the hook's key a request must be signed with, a positive whole number of at most nine digits. Raising it revokes the key before it. It is not a secret.

perHour.description: The most fires governor queues for the hook in one clock hour, a positive whole number up to 100. A fire past it gets 429. Default 20.

ticketReviews.description: The ticket reviews governor runs, in file order, each with its `name`, its selector `when`, the labels each of its `conclusions` adds, and optionally its own `checklist` and checks and labels per ticket type (`types`). Each comments on a ticket it selects whether it passes, waits for an edit, or waits for a person, and applies that conclusion's labels. At least one when the `ticketReviews` switch is on.

name.description: The review's name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the list. It goes into every comment and marker the review writes, so renaming a review starts its rounds afresh.

on.description: The event that runs the review. Only `"opened"`: an open issue opened, reopened or with its body edited.

labels.description: Labels the ticket must carry, every one of them, in any case. Default none.

exclude.description: Labels the ticket must not carry, any of them, in any case. Default none.

by.description: Who may have opened the ticket, as GitHub's `author_association` values. Default `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR`. The repo's `trust.review` bounds every review.

when.description: The review's selector: `on`, the event, and the labels and authors a ticket must meet.

conclusions.description: The labels each conclusion adds: `success`, `failure` and `neutral`, each a list, each none when unset. Each run adds its conclusion's labels and removes the ones the other two name, and touches no other label. Each label starts with the review's name, a colon and a space, such as `triage: build` for a review named `triage`, in any case, so a review never adds or removes a label a person uses. A label appears under one conclusion of one review. A review whose `by`, within `trust.review`, reaches beyond `trust.auto` names no ready label. No conclusion names a label a `types` entry matches on, a label the review's own `when.labels` or `when.exclude` names, or `labels.claim`.

success.description: The labels a `success` adds: the ticket passes. Default none.

failure.description: The labels a `failure` adds: the ticket waits for an edit by whoever filed it. Default none.

neutral.description: The labels a `neutral` adds: the ticket waits for a person. Default none.

checklist.description: The review's base checklist, after governor's fixed frame: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Default governor's own checklist.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

types.description: Checks and labels per ticket type, each entry matched by label. A ticket gets the base checklist and then each matching entry's, in file order; one matching none gets the base alone. For each conclusion, the labels come from the first matching entry that names it, and otherwise from `conclusions`.

labels.description: The labels that match a ticket carrying any of them, in any case. At least one.

checklist.description: Checks a matching ticket gets after the review's base checklist: the text, or { "file": "<path>" }. Default none.

file.description: The file holding the text: a path in the repo, from its root, read from the default branch beside the config file. A skill file's frontmatter is dropped.

conclusions.description: The conclusions whose labels this entry overrides, each a list, each label starting with the review's name, a colon and a space. A conclusion it leaves out takes its labels from an entry later in the file that matches, or from the review's `conclusions`.

success.description: The labels a `success` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.

failure.description: The labels a `failure` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.

neutral.description: The labels a `neutral` adds on a matching ticket, in place of the review's.
